quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #21
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: Which factor does NOT affect how far it takes to stop your vehicle?

options.text: Steering ability
Braking distance
Reaction distance
Perception time

questions.correctAnswerText: Steering ability
questions.explanation: Stopping distance depends on perception time, reaction distance, and braking distance. These change based on your speed and road conditions.

questions.question: A red flashing traffic light means the same thing as a:

options.text: Solid red light.
Stop sign.
Yield sign.
Caution sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop sign.
questions.explanation: A red flashing traffic light means the same as a stop sign. Come to a complete stop and go only when it is safe.

questions.question: If an accident causes injury, death, or $1,000 or more in damage, you must report it to police within ____ days.

options.text: Two days
Four days
Five days
10 days

questions.correctAnswerText: Four days
questions.explanation: You must complete an accident report form within four days if the accident caused injury, death, or $1,000 or more in damage and police did not file a report.

questions.question: When driving a slow vehicle in a no passing zone on a two-lane road, you should pull over to let others pass if:

options.text: One vehicle is behind you.
Two or more vehicles form a line behind you and it's unsafe for them to pass.
Five or more vehicles form a line behind you and it's unsafe for them to pass.
The road has slow-moving vehicle signs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Five or more vehicles form a line behind you and it's unsafe for them to pass.
questions.explanation: If five or more vehicles are behind you on a two-lane road where passing is unsafe, you must pull over and stop to let them pass if it is safe to do so.

questions.question: A slow-moving vehicle emblem is:

options.text: A rectangular red sign.
A circular green sign.
A diamond-shaped yellow sign.
A triangular orange sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: A triangular orange sign.
questions.explanation: A slow-moving vehicle emblem is a reflective orange triangle. Vehicles with this symbol travel at 25 mph or slower.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: The left lane is only for vehicles with a certain number of people.
Specific turning movements are allowed from specific lanes.
Do not enter.
Drivers in both lanes must merge smoothly.

questions.correctAnswerText: The left lane is only for vehicles with a certain number of people.
questions.explanation: This sign marks a high occupancy vehicle (HOV) lane. HOV lanes are for buses and cars with a driver and one or more passengers, as shown on the sign.

questions.question: What is the best way to stay safe when backing your vehicle?

options.text: Honk your horn right before shifting into reverse.
Check behind the vehicle before you get in the driver's seat.
Check your rearview mirrors to see what is behind you.
Turn up the radio to get the attention of people around you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check behind the vehicle before you get in the driver's seat.
questions.explanation: Backing is dangerous because drivers cannot see well behind their vehicles. Before backing up, walk behind the vehicle to check for children and small objects.

questions.question: Do not park within:

options.text: 10 feet of a fire hydrant.
15 feet of a fire hydrant.
20 feet of a fire hydrant.
30 feet of a fire hydrant.

questions.correctAnswerText: 15 feet of a fire hydrant.
questions.explanation: You cannot park within 15 feet of a fire hydrant.

questions.question: Pennant-shaped signs mean:

options.text: School zones.
No passing zones.
Speed limits.
Railroad crossings.

questions.correctAnswerText: No passing zones.
questions.explanation: Pennant-shaped signs show no passing zones. The sign will also have text to confirm it is a no passing zone.

questions.question: Pentagonal signs mean:

options.text: No passing zones.
School zones.
Speed limits.
Railroad crossings.

questions.correctAnswerText: School zones.
questions.explanation: Pentagonal signs show you are in a school zone. Watch carefully for children and pedestrians when driving near a school.

questions.question: When driving to an unfamiliar area, you should:

options.text: Depend on road signs to find your way.
Plan your trip in advance.
Only know generally where your destination is.
Always choose the most direct route.

questions.correctAnswerText: Plan your trip in advance.
questions.explanation: Plan your trip before you drive. Know where you are going. Check the location on a map before you start driving.

questions.question: You should be alert to motorcycles because:

options.text: They are harder to see than cars.
They rarely use their headlights.
Motorcyclists are less skilled drivers than other drivers.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: They are harder to see than cars.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles are smaller and harder to see than cars. They can hide in your blind spot. It is hard to judge how far away a motorcycle is and how fast it is going. Always watch for motorcycles and be extra careful around them.

questions.question: If an oncoming driver does not dim their high beams, where should you look?

options.text: At the wheels of the approaching vehicle.
Toward the right side of the road.
Toward the left side of the road.
Straight down the middle of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Toward the right side of the road.
questions.explanation: Look toward the right side of the road. This keeps you from being blinded and lets you see the road ahead until the other vehicle passes.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Bicycle crossing.
Stop.
Fines double in a work zone.
Stop ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Bicycle crossing.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. They alert you to road hazards ahead. This sign warns you that bicycles may cross the road.

questions.question: When you see this black and yellow sign, it means:

options.text: The road to the right is one-way only.
There is a detour to the right because of roadwork.
Slow down because the road ahead turns sharply.
There is a crossroad to your right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down because the road ahead turns sharply.
questions.explanation: This sign tells you the road ahead turns sharply. Slow down before the curve, like you would at a sharp intersection turn.

questions.question: Regulatory signs are usually ____ and must always be obeyed.

options.text: White
Blue
Green
Orange

questions.correctAnswerText: White
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs control traffic. They are white with black markings. All drivers must obey them.

questions.question: If an oncoming driver is heading toward you in your lane, you should:

options.text: Honk, steer right, and speed up.
Honk, steer left, and brake.
Honk, steer right, and brake.
Stay in the center, honk, and brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Honk, steer right, and brake.
questions.explanation: Honk to get the other driver's attention. If they don't move, steer right to escape. Do not steer left because they might also move left and you will still crash. Brake firmly and steadily. Every mile per hour you slow reduces the impact.

questions.question: When two vehicles enter an intersection at the same time from different roads, which vehicle must yield?

options.text: Either one
The vehicle on the left
The vehicle on the right
Neither

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle on the left
questions.explanation: At any intersection, when two vehicles arrive at the same time, the vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.

questions.question: When turning left in an intersection, drivers:

options.text: Can wait in the intersection until it is safe to turn left.
Can wait in the intersection until the light turns yellow to turn left.
Must wait for a green arrow before turning left.
Must not enter an intersection unless they can get through without stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must not enter an intersection unless they can get through without stopping.
questions.explanation: Do not enter an intersection unless you can get through it without stopping. When turning left, wait for oncoming traffic and pedestrians to clear so you do not block the intersection when the light turns red.

questions.question: When you see a steady yellow arrow, you should:

options.text: Merge into the lane the arrow is pointing to.
Slow down and stop, if it is safe to do so.
Turn left after yielding to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
Have the right-of-way and oncoming traffic must stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and stop, if it is safe to do so.
questions.explanation: A steady yellow arrow means a red arrow is coming next. Stop unless you are already in the intersection.

questions.question: What is a speed limit?

options.text: The highest or lowest legal speed you can drive on a road when conditions are dangerous.
The highest or lowest legal speed you can drive on a road when conditions are ideal.
The recommended speed to drive on a road when conditions are ideal.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: The highest or lowest legal speed you can drive on a road when conditions are ideal.
questions.explanation: A speed limit is the highest or lowest legal speed you can drive on a road when conditions are ideal. You can drive slower than the posted speed, but you cannot drive faster. You must drive slower in school zones and work zones. If conditions like road construction or bad weather make the posted speed unsafe, drive slower.

questions.question: Which suggestion does NOT help with safe night driving?

options.text: Keep your windshield clean.
Know that tinted windows reduce visibility at night.
Carry a flashlight in your vehicle.
Look directly at the headlights of oncoming vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look directly at the headlights of oncoming vehicles.
questions.explanation: When you look directly at oncoming headlights, your eyes contract to protect themselves. After the vehicle passes, your eyes need time to adjust back to the darkness. During this time, you cannot see well and are essentially driving blind.

questions.question: When can you cross solid yellow lines?

options.text: To pass traffic moving in the same direction.
During the day only.
Anytime.
When you are making a turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you are making a turn.
questions.explanation: Broken lines can be crossed, but solid lines cannot. You can cross a solid yellow line only when you are turning.

questions.question: You are in the left lane and want to move to the right lane. What should you do?

options.text: Check mirrors, signal, and look over your left shoulder before changing lanes.
Check mirrors, signal, and look over your right shoulder before changing lanes.
Check mirrors, signal, and look over both shoulders before changing lanes.
Check mirrors, signal, and change lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check mirrors, signal, and look over your right shoulder before changing lanes.
questions.explanation: When changing lanes, look over your shoulder in the direction you want to move to check your blind spot. Always check your mirrors and turn on your signal before changing lanes.

questions.question: What does a solid red arrow in a traffic signal mean?

options.text: It is never used in traffic signals.
It means the same thing as a red circular traffic light.
Drivers may turn in the direction the arrow points.
Traffic in that direction must stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: It means the same thing as a red circular traffic light.
questions.explanation: A solid red arrow means the same as a red circular traffic light. When you see a red arrow, you must stop and cannot turn in the direction the arrow points.
